source: the spec step's run PS (build/p362/SPEC.md §2.1, scratch/p362/spec/fixtures-raw/PS): events.jsonl and fault-trace.tsv byte for byte as recorded; app.log as recorded less the lines that name his home (the login PATH capture) and the boot.env records; the rest below is the spec step's recorded reading or, under "constructed", made from it

constructed.addEvents: the spec step's recorder did not wrap the app:quit invoke or each window's send; its own app.quit lines told the renderer's quit apart by its stack, and its menu-quit line named the window the parent's rule picks (settings), so these lines say what that recorder could not: hooked, the invoke wrapped, and where the quit event went THE PROBE REVIEW: and one `fallback-armed` line 1 ms after the press. Every press of the Quit row arms requestQuit’s 3 s timer at both builds (src/main/menu.ts), the recorder this probe writes logs that arming, and the spec step’s did not; without the line, “no fallback quit” could not be asked of these runs.
constructed.snapshots: the folder's names and each live id's completion record, made from the recorded counts: 8 of 8 shells with an app-quit record after the press, 8 bodies written after it, 0 .part left (the .part pattern is the recorded partNames')
constructed.backups: the backup index, made from the recorded newest generation (quit)
constructed.tracker: the tracker did not exist at the spec step (SPEC D11); these lines are its shape for a quit that ended by the will-quit SIGKILL: open at will-quit, no quit and no exit, a read only gate connection closed and an arch.db one beside it THE PROBE REVIEW: and the `state-hooked` line the tracker writes once its will-quit and quit listeners are in.
constructed.shim: the recorded tail of the launch’s output and its exit code
constructed.exitAt: the press plus the recorded "process gone" time
